subject: general
question: During which of the following movements did Mahatma Gandhi give the slogan 'Do or Die'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Quit India Movement**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan **'Do or Die'** during the **Quit India Movement**.
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched on **8th August 1942**, during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• This movement was a significant milestone in the Indian independence struggle, marked by widespread protests and demonstrations.
 
• Gandhi's call for 'Do or Die' symbolized the determination and urgency of the Indian people to achieve independence.
 
• The British government responded with mass arrests and repression, but the movement intensified the demand for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Non-Cooperation Movement** was launched by Gandhi in 1920 to resist British rule through non-violent means.
 
• The **Ghadar Movement** was an early 20th-century anti-colonial effort by expatriate Indians to overthrow British rule.
 
• The **Home Rule Movement**, led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant, sought self-governance for India within the British Empire.
 
• The Quit India Movement is also known as the **August Movement** due to its launch in August 1942.
 
• Despite its immediate suppression, the Quit India Movement laid the groundwork for India’s eventual independence in 1947.
